title: Mamanock Neck
summary: Mamanock names a neck of land at East Moriches in Brookhaven. The cited records place Mamanock with Meritces, or Moriches Neck, suggesting a connected pair of necks along the south shore.
address_label: General Mamanock Neck / East Moriches shoreline, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general East Moriches neck point based on Tooker's Mamanock and Meritces/Moriches Neck context; offset from Kitchaminchok/Moriches Island marker for visibility and not an exact neck boundary.
why_this_matters: The discovery of an longstanding Woodland-period quartz arrowhead workshop and scattered pottery fragments on Mamanock Neck reveals that this coastal area south of East Moriches was a highly productive manufacturing hub. Unearthing such specialized workspaces demonstrates that early Long Island Indigenous communities established places for craft, resource use, and daily life.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as land united or joined to another tract. Because the source points toward Moriches, the name belongs alongside Meritces or Moriches Neck.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names and associated stories about these places illustrate community histories, lifeways, and cultural ethics and practices that are grounded in people’s intimate relationships with their homeland.”

— Richard Stoffle, Kathleen Van Vlack, Simon Larsson, Yoko Kugo, Steve Baumann, and Alex Wolfson, Name It and Its Yours: Toponym Disputes Between Native and Settler Colonials in North America (2026), Article discussion of place names and associated stories
artifacts_content: Archaeological sources describe decorated and grit-tempered pottery fragments, quartz flakes, and fire-cracked rock in the broader area, suggesting long-term human activity around Mamanock Neck.
land_loss_content: Mamanock preserves a local geography of adjoining necks at East Moriches. It shows how Indigenous placenames in deeds and surveys described relationships between tracts, not only isolated points on a map.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general East Moriches shoreline point for Mamanock Neck. It does not trace the full neck boundary or the adjoining Moriches/Meritces tract.
